About

From analysis to hardware

I'm an aerospace engineering student double-majoring in mechanical at the University at Buffalo, graduating May 2027. My work runs from aerodynamics through structures to physical test — this past summer I designed hardware for a Mach 0.2–1.3 transonic wind tunnel at Calspan Corporation, including a Schlieren imaging camera mount and alignment system built to minimize vibration, and this spring I developed ANSYS CFD models of electrohydrodynamic jetting in a university interfacial-phenomena lab. Coursework has taken me through UAV wing optimization, XFLR5 airfoil validation against thin airfoil theory, an Arduino quadcopter attitude controller, and a structural FEA study converged to within 0.06%. I like problems that end in a drawing, a test, and a number.
